newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Ecuador launches long-awaited debut Eurobond.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Ecuador launches long-awaited debut Eurobond.

text.p: Ecuador tapped the Eurobond market for the first time on Friday with a well-received $500 million deal, lead underwriter Chase said on Friday.
"It's been a long time coming," syndicate manager at Chase said. "We've been working hard to build up a book and to ensure Ecuador's debut is a success," he added.
"We have a very large over-subscribed book with broad distribution across Europe and the U.S. with both retail and institutional interest."
Ecuador has no credit ratings, but the syndicate manager said while it was unusual for a sovereign to launch an unrated deal, Chase felt it was unnecessary for this transaction.
Other sources close to the deal were not as upbeat.
"The bonds are cheap compared to some of the other benchmarks out there, but compared to the Bradies its expensive," a syndicate manager in the group said, adding Ecuador was a poor credit.
"Chase have only syndicated 10 to 12 percent of this deal, so they have a pretty good strangle-hold on it," he said.

The mandate for the transaction was awarded in November last year, but launch was delayed due to political uncertainty in the Ecuador, generally difficult market conditions and volatility in emerging markets, dealers said.
Abdala Bucaram was elected president in July, but Congress removed him in February 1997 and elected Fabian Alarcon as interim president until August 1998.

Ecuador's two-tranche Eurobond totals $500 million. The five-year fixed-rate tranche, for $350 million, was priced to yield 470 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes. It pays a coupon of 11.25 percent.
The seven-year floating rate tranche, for $150 million, pays a coupon of six-month LIBOR plus 475 b.p.
"The structure was used in response to investor demand," the syndicate manager at Chase said, adding the five-year maturity was sought after.
Ecuador's Brady bonds -- rescheduled debt turned into interest-bearing bonds -- were boosted by the transaction, dealers said.
Ecuador's most liquid benchmark bond, the PDI rose 3/4 to trade at 57-3/4 bid at 1500 GMT.
